sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: Claude reads CLAUDE.md files at the start of every session; Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration; to block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook; target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file; files over 200 lines consume more context and may reduce adherence; run /init to generate a starting CLAUDE.md

beats.spoken: What does Claude Code know about your project before it opens a single file? Two real runs, one question.
The test folder only holds a README, and the README says nothing about a server. For the second run, a CLAUDE.md is added, with exactly one made-up fact: the name of the test server.
According to the docs, Claude reads this file at the start of every session. The question about the server shows whether that holds. That fact exists nowhere else in the folder.

data.quote: Claude reads them at the start of every session.
data.translation: Read at the start of every session.

beats.spoken: Run one, no CLAUDE.md. Claude searched four times with Grep and Glob, for test server, for server and host, and for all files. It found nothing and could not name the server.

Run two, with a CLAUDE.md. Claude answered right away, without a single tool, and named kranich-07. The whole run took about nine seconds, and the answer pointed to the project CLAUDE.md as its source.

Both runs ran twice, with the same result. Whatever is in the CLAUDE.md was there from the start. Both repetitions of the second run answered the same way. Without the file, Claude found the fact in no repetition. According to the docs, the init command writes a first draft.

data.headline: 2 runs, twice each
data.note: First draft: /init (per the docs, not recorded here).

beats.spoken: So whatever Claude should know every time belongs in the CLAUDE.md. Follow Promptwerk for more Claude workflows, step by step.

data.statement: What Claude should always know: in CLAUDE.md.
